name: Should I choose MDF or solid wood trim for door casing?

mainEntity.name: Should I choose MDF or solid wood trim for door casing?

acceptedAnswer.text: The decision between MDF (medium-density fiberboard) and solid wood comes down to finish preference and room environment. MDF provides a smooth, knot-free surface that takes paint evenly without warping, making it a cost-effective option for painted trim in bedrooms and hallways. Solid pine, poplar, or hardwood is necessary if you intend to stain the wood, and solid wood withstands heavy impacts far better than MDF. In high-moisture spaces like bathrooms, solid wood or moisture-resistant trim is generally preferable because standard MDF can swell if exposed to standing water or high humidity.
acceptedAnswer.description: Choose MDF for affordable, smooth painted finishes in dry living areas; choose solid wood if you plan to stain the trim or need greater moisture and impact resistance in wet areas.
